account:
Today I have been following my appointments: morning office business, the ten o'clock mill inspection, and now lunch at home. Council letters are due at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at the east-dock cottage at fifteen, and Builder's office review at sixteen thirty.

The unusual thing is repeated talk among townsfolk about a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Several people repeat nearly identical reports naming Baker and my neighbour, and mentioning Baker carrying a sack of bread. I have not seen a change to the bridge or port, nor heard a clear description of one. A sack of bread is not itself evidence of anything unusual for Baker. I asked my neighbour what had changed and whether Freight had a concern, but received no substantive answer that I could hear. I cannot yet tell whether this is a real transport issue or simply a rumour spreading through town.

At the mill stall I saw 128 hay bales. I did not locate a keeper who could confirm storage conditions or delivery reliability, so my inspection establishes stock on hand, not that the whole supply chain is sound.

Secretary is arranging a written record of Builder's findings for this afternoon. I handed over one emerald for a writable office book, separately from the agreed two-emerald inspection fee, though Secretary subsequently said her purse was empty and asked for it again. That discrepancy needs clarification rather than an assumption of wrongdoing. Yesterday's written report found no confirmed defects and recommended no repair spending without an identified need. I understand today's paperwork and meeting to be for documenting the inspection and deciding whether any specific maintenance is justified. No bread order for town hall has been authorized.
